nb9bbb4d15b5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about suspension-related rules in the Lok Sabha?
o: Rule 373 – Member directed to withdraw for the day
Rule 373 – Automatic suspension for five sittings for grave disorder
Rule 374 – Suspension by a House motion up to the remainder of the session
Rule 374A – Automatic suspension for grave disorder
nb9bbb4d15b5.x: Automatic suspension for grave disorder is under Rule 374A; Rule 373 only directs a member to withdraw for the day.

ncfaf140ed42.s:
Assertion (A): As per the PRS Annual Review of State Laws 2025, many State Assemblies met only to satisfy a constitutional requirement.
Reason (R): Article 174 bars a gap of more than six months between two sessions.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ncfaf140ed42.x: PRS found many Assemblies (average about 24 sitting days) met only to meet the Article 174 six-month rule, so R explains A.

n96dc82d0885.s: The proposed enlargement of the Lok Sabha would raise its strength from 550 to how many seats?
n96dc82d0885.x: The proposal increases the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850 seats, raising the Lok Sabha–Rajya Sabha ratio from 2.2:1 to 3.3:1.

n279bcada197.s: The Lok Sabha generally sits for about how many days in a year?
n279bcada197.x: The Lok Sabha sits around 60–70 days a year, whereas the UK House of Commons has more than 150 sittings.

nf1453fe213a.s: The 86th All India Presiding Officers' Conference (AIPOC) was held at:
nf1453fe213a.x: The 86th AIPOC was held at Lucknow with the theme 'Strong Legislature - Prosperous Nation'.

nbace7c9d1f9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the Indian and British parliamentary systems?
o: The Indian Parliament is bound by a written Constitution and judicial review
The British Parliament is subject to the basic structure doctrine
India has an elected head of state
Britain has a hereditary monarch as head of state
nbace7c9d1f9.x: The basic structure doctrine belongs to the Indian constitutional framework and does not govern the British Parliament.

nee232b5947c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's adoption of the parliamentary form of government?
o: India's size and diversity favoured a system of continuous political accommodation
The Constituent Assembly sought to avoid a personality cult around a single executive
Dr B.R. Ambedkar held that a democracy cannot maximise both stability and responsibility
The parliamentary form guarantees both maximum stability and continuous accountability
nee232b5947c.x: Ambedkar stated that a democracy cannot maximise stability and responsibility simultaneously, so the parliamentary form does not guarantee both.

n9d447acba39.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Shamsher Singh (1974)?
o: It held public criticism of Cabinet policy by the Governor compatible with parliamentary conventions
It connected the Governor's conduct with the logic of the parliamentary system
It is relevant to the limits parliamentary responsibility places on constitutional office-holders
n9d447acba39.x: Public criticism of Cabinet policy by the Governor was held to run counter to the parliamentary system.

n4c55d698727.s: In India, the residuary powers of legislation are vested in:
o: Both Parliament and the States concurrently
n4c55d698727.x: India vests residuary powers in Parliament, whereas the United States leaves the remaining powers to the States.

n1a6a23d5e60.s: France's Fifth Republic was established in:

nba59bc0bf03.s: Which of the following is a feature of the presidential system?
o: A fixed term for the executive
Executive accountable to the legislature as in a parliamentary system
A plural executive headed by a Prime Minister
Fusion of executive and legislative powers
nba59bc0bf03.x: A presidential system generally has a single, directly elected executive with a fixed term, not accountable to the legislature in the parliamentary sense.

n99c18ceaa8b.s: Who is the Leader of the Lok Sabha (Leader of the House) and the chief spokesperson of the Government?
n99c18ceaa8b.x: The Prime Minister leads the majority in the Lok Sabha, is Leader of the House and the Government's chief spokesperson; the President is Head of State.

n86e875a1583.s: Which of the following is a demerit of the presidential system?
o: Frequent fall of governments through no-confidence motions
n86e875a1583.x: Executive-legislature deadlock (and a personality cult around a single executive) are demerits of the presidential system; it has a fixed tenure.

nc583603c290.s: Which of the following is a merit of the parliamentary system?
o: A fixed tenure for the executive
Continuous accountability of the executive to the legislature
nc583603c290.x: Continuous accountability of the executive to the legislature is a merit of the parliamentary system; fixed tenure is not its feature.

n2e561830fe3.s: In the Indian parliamentary system, who provides central leadership to the Council of Ministers?
n2e561830fe3.x: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers; the President is only the nominal head of the executive.

nbecc18cd08f.s: Which of the following features is associated with Britain but not with India in the same form?
o: Collective responsibility to the lower House
nbecc18cd08f.x: Britain has an institutionalised shadow cabinet, legal ministerial responsibility and ministers who must be MPs; India lacks these in the same form.

n82255221a5f.s: In which year did the United States adopt the 22nd Amendment, associated with limiting presidential tenure?
n82255221a5f.x: The US adopted the 22nd Amendment in 1951; India has no term limit for its Prime Minister.

nb6115a406a8.s: The parliamentary system of government is based on:
o: Fusion of executive and legislative powers
nb6115a406a8.x: The parliamentary system rests on fusion of executive and legislative powers, while the presidential system rests on separation of powers.

n9315a4c3060.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the ordinance-making powers of the Governor and the President?
o: The Governor's ordinance power extends to the State and Concurrent Lists
The Governor may promulgate an ordinance when the State Legislature is not in session
Ordinances cease six weeks after the Legislature or Parliament reassembles
The President's ordinance power extends only to the Union List
n9315a4c3060.x: The President's ordinance power is co-extensive with Parliament's legislative power, including the Concurrent List.

nd4d5d93cb78.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Governor's immunity under Article 361?
o: The Governor is not answerable to any court for official acts
The Governor cannot be arrested or imprisoned during the term of office
Civil proceedings concerning personal acts require two months' notice
Criminal proceedings can be instituted during the term with prior permission of the High Court
nd4d5d93cb78.x: No criminal proceedings can be instituted against the Governor during the term, even with a court's prior permission.

nc5860f14226.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 201?
o: Even after reconsideration, the President is not bound to assent
The President may direct the Governor to return a non-Money Bill for reconsideration
The Constitution fixes a period within which the President must decide every reserved Bill
The President may withhold assent to a Bill reserved by the Governor
nc5860f14226.x: Article 201 prescribes no fixed time limit for the President's decision on a reserved Bill.

nd9124119e78.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Punchhi Commission – Fixed tenure for the Governor
Sarkaria Commission – Politically neutral outsider as Governor and consultation with the CM
First ARC – Fixed tenure for the Governor
Rajamannar Committee – Review of Centre-State relations; recommendations not implemented
nd9124119e78.x: Fixed tenure for the Governor was the Punchhi Commission's recommendation; the First ARC stressed long public experience and a non-partisan attitude.

na4e26cabba2.s: Which of the following pairs of Bills reserved for the President and the relevant Article is wrongly matched?
o: Concurrent List Bill repugnant to a central law – Article 254(2)
Money Bills during a Financial Emergency – Article 360
Taxes on water or electricity in inter-State river projects – Article 304(b)
na4e26cabba2.x: Taxes on water/electricity in inter-State river projects fall under Article 288; Article 304(b) concerns restrictions on inter-State trade.

n1a60d261b98.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the November 2025 Presidential Reference opinion?
o: The President need not seek the Supreme Court's advice on each reserved Bill
Judicial review is limited to issues such as mala fides and procedure
Courts may impose a fixed deadline for every Bill pending before a Governor
n1a60d261b98.x: The opinion rejected court-imposed timelines, permitting only limited intervention in cases of prolonged unexplained inaction.

n75424f7b42e.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
n75424f7b42e.s: The First ARC study team on Centre-State relations recommended an Inter-State Council under Article:
n75424f7b42e.x: The study team recommended an Inter-State Council under Article 263, along with non-partisan Governors, delegation of powers and more resources for States.

n91d0a761e29.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a State Bill reserved for the President under Article 201?
o: A returned Bill must be reconsidered by the State Legislature within six months
The President may direct the Governor to return even a Money Bill for reconsideration
The President is not bound to assent even after the Bill is passed again
Article 201 prescribes no fixed time limit for the President's decision
n91d0a761e29.x: Only a non-Money Bill can be returned to the State Legislature for reconsideration.

n8f45301939d.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Appointment of the State PSC Chairman and members – Article 316
All executive action of the State Government – Article 165
Appointment of the Chief Minister and Ministers – Article 164
n8f45301939d.x: Executive action in the Governor's name is under Article 166; Article 165 concerns the Advocate-General.

n199b3d16168.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Council of Ministers?
o: A non-member may be a Minister but must become an MLA or MLC within six months
State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Chief Minister
The Governor appoints the Chief Minister, normally the Assembly majority leader
Article 164 deals with the State Council of Ministers
n199b3d16168.x: State Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, not the Chief Minister.

nc6a11b6f8cc.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Reserving a Bill for the President – Article 200
Administration of an adjoining Union Territory – Article 239
Seeking information from the Chief Minister – Article 239
nc6a11b6f8cc.x: The Governor seeks information from the Chief Minister under Article 167; Article 239 concerns administration of Union Territories.

n4a28104e450.s: Under the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a State Council of Ministers including the CM cannot exceed what share of the Assembly's total strength?
n4a28104e450.x: The ceiling is 15% of the Legislative Assembly's total strength, with a minimum of 12 (Art. 164(1A)).

n186a5e1f865.s: The Sarkaria Commission recommended that Article 356 be used:
o: As the first response to political instability
n186a5e1f865.x: Sarkaria recommended Article 356 only as a last resort, along with a mandatory floor test and a politically neutral outsider as Governor.

n45c75f0f7b8.s: Bills reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President are dealt with under Article:
n45c75f0f7b8.x: Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the President; Article 200 covers the Governor's choices on a State Bill.

n54a0567c6cc.s: Who became Governor of Andhra Pradesh in February 2023?
n54a0567c6cc.x: S. Abdul Nazeer has been Governor of Andhra Pradesh since February 2023.

n15cde251e18.s: The Punchhi Commission recommended a localised emergency in a district for up to:
n15cde251e18.x: Punchhi recommended a localised district emergency for up to three months, codification of Bommai guidelines and fixed tenure for Governors.

n62958ecacee.s: A Governor holds office during the pleasure of the:
n62958ecacee.x: Article 156 incorporates the President's pleasure, though B.P. Singhal held it cannot be exercised arbitrarily.

n47c44ad14db.s: The Governor's special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year is under Article:
n47c44ad14db.x: The special address under Article 176 is mandatory on both occasions and is delivered on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

n89236b60992.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that summoning, proroguing and dissolving the Assembly under Article 174 are not discretionary powers of the Governor?
n89236b60992.x: Nabam Rebia held these powers and the address under Articles 175–176 are exercised on aid and advice, rejecting a general discretion.

nb32fc5edd19.s: Under Article 174, not more than ____ may intervene between two sessions of a State Legislature.
nb32fc5edd19.x: Article 174 bars a gap of more than six months between two sessions.

nf92413064d2.s: In a hung State Assembly, the Sarkaria and Punchhi approach gives first preference for forming the government to:
o: A post-poll alliance with outside support
nf92413064d2.x: The order is pre-poll alliance, largest party with support, post-poll coalition, then post-poll alliance with outside support.

n43434021f2d.s: Which provision bars courts from inquiring into the advice tendered by Ministers to the Governor?
n43434021f2d.x: Article 163(3) bars courts from inquiring into ministers' advice; Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on discretion final.

n8ad26b65fbd.s: The qualifications of a Governor are laid down in Article:
n8ad26b65fbd.x: Article 157 deals with qualifications; 155 with appointment, 156 with tenure and 158 with conditions of office.

n7a297da7f96.s: Which case held that an Assembly should not be dissolved before Parliament approves a proclamation under Article 356?
n7a297da7f96.x: Bommai protected the Assembly pending parliamentary approval, allowed restoration of a displaced ministry and treated secularism as a basic feature.

nindian-polity-74-4.s: The Governor's ordinance-making power is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-74-4.x: The Governor's ordinances are under Article 213 (State and Concurrent subjects); the President's under Article 123.

nindian-polity-11-18.s: The Governor's pardoning power, limited to offences against State laws, is under Article:
nindian-polity-11-18.x: The Governor pardons under Article 161 (State laws only); the President under Article 72 (all cases).

n34bbfc53d32.s: To extend President's Rule beyond one year, a National Emergency must be in operation and elections must be certified as impossible by the:
n34bbfc53d32.x: Beyond one year, a National Emergency must be in force and the Election Commission must certify that elections cannot be held.

nf37df593ac1.s: The Governor's special responsibility for law and order in Arunachal Pradesh is provided under Article:
nf37df593ac1.x: Article 371H gives the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh law and order responsibility; Article 371A does so for Nagaland.

n5d8c597b38d.s: The latest spell of President's Rule in Manipur began on:
n5d8c597b38d.x: The latest spell began on 13 February 2025 (Manipur's 11th) and was revoked on 4 February 2026.

n6b5fe203c7f.s: Which case rejected the dissolution of an Assembly based on unproven fears of horse-trading?
n6b5fe203c7f.x: Rameshwar Prasad (2006) rejected dissolution on unproven fears of horse-trading.

n9203ebd3232.s: By convention, before a Governor is appointed, who is consulted?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
The Chief Minister of the State
n9203ebd3232.x: By convention the Governor is generally an outsider and the State's Chief Minister is consulted; the Constitution does not mandate this.

n8dcee2f54d7.s: Reservation by the Governor for the President is mandatory for a Bill that:
o: Derogates from the powers of the High Court
n8dcee2f54d7.x: A Bill derogating from the High Court's powers must be reserved; not every Bill affecting State finances needs mandatory reservation.

n2dfafe3e926.s: President's Rule under Article 356 was first imposed in 1951 in:
n2dfafe3e926.x: President's Rule was first imposed in Punjab in 1951; Kerala (1959) saw the first dismissal of an elected government.

n72ca9480c4b.s: The emoluments of a Governor are determined by:
n72ca9480c4b.x: Under Article 158, a Governor's emoluments are fixed by Parliament by law, not by the State Legislature.

n6f1a51a86fb.s: The maximum period for which President's Rule can ordinarily continue is:
n6f1a51a86fb.x: President's Rule continues six months at a time with parliamentary approval, up to a maximum of three years.

n986d6791b7e.s: The CAG's report relating to a State is placed before the State Legislature by the:
n986d6791b7e.x: The Governor places the CAG report on the State, along with the State PSC and State Finance Commission reports, before the Legislature.

nafdb25d8ee9.s: After the Ayodhya events of December 1992, BJP governments of Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and ____ were dismissed.
nafdb25d8ee9.x: The BJP governments of UP, MP, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh were removed; Bommai upheld the dismissals of MP, Rajasthan and HP.

n76a8d818afa.s: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in:
n76a8d818afa.x: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in 1969, before Sarkaria (1983), NCRWC (2000) and Punchhi (2007).

n3d9a2253c9f.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sarkaria and Punchhi order of preference for inviting a group to form the government in a hung Assembly?
o: A post-poll coalition comes before the single largest party with support
A post-poll alliance with outside support comes last
A pre-poll alliance gets first preference
The single largest party with support of others comes second
n3d9a2253c9f.x: The order is pre-poll alliance, single largest party with support, post-poll coalition, then post-poll alliance with outside support.

nc1855be2546.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
nc1855be2546.s: Under Article 167, who is the chief link between the Governor and the State Council of Ministers?
nc1855be2546.x: Article 167 makes the Chief Minister the link, communicating Council decisions to the Governor and placing matters before the Council when required.

n1733e5f37f9.s: The term of office of the Chief Minister is:
n1733e5f37f9.x: The Constitution does not fix the Chief Minister's term.

n6bb8fbc0908.s: Under the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025, a PM, CM or Minister in custody for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five years or more is removed on the:
n6bb8fbc0908.x: The Bill (amending Articles 75, 164 and 239AA) provides removal on the 31st day after 30 consecutive days in custody.

nindian-polity-10-6.s: Who was the first woman Chief Minister in India?
nindian-polity-10-6.x: Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister; E.M.S. Namboodiripad was the first non-Congress Chief Minister.

n628d720ccfa.s: The office of Deputy Chief Minister in a State is:
o: A political arrangement not specifically mentioned in the Constitution
n628d720ccfa.x: The Constitution does not specifically mention the office; the incumbent is sworn in as a minister and the post is a political arrangement.

n0491ffdf31e.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
n0491ffdf31e.s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly can be removed by a resolution of a majority of all the then members after a notice of:
n0491ffdf31e.x: Under Article 179, removal requires a resolution by a majority of all the then members after fourteen days' notice.

nindian-polity-62-14.s: Which of the following is NOT a field for nomination by the Governor to the State Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-62-14.x: The valid fields are literature, science, art, the co-operative movement and social service; industrial activity is not one.

n48a6495bf7b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of a State Legislative Council?
o: One-third are elected by local bodies
One-twelfth are elected by teachers of three years' standing
One-sixth are elected by registered graduates
One-sixth are nominated by the Governor
n48a6495bf7b.x: Registered graduates elect one-twelfth; the one-sixth share is nominated by the Governor.

na758d0f88e0.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
na758d0f88e0.s: MLAs elect what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
na758d0f88e0.x: MLAs elect one-third of the Council's members; they also vote in Presidential and Rajya Sabha elections.

nindian-polity-40-56.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a State Money Bill?
o: The Speaker's certification of a Money Bill is final
The Legislative Council may permanently block it
The Governor's recommendation is required before its introduction
The Legislative Council may keep it for 14 days
nindian-polity-40-56.x: The Council cannot block a Money Bill; it can only keep it for 14 days.

ndb5b4ef956b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about State Legislative Councils?
o: A Council gives a place to experts who cannot face elections
Its existence depends on the ruling party in the Assembly, as in Andhra Pradesh
A Council can permanently veto an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly
ndb5b4ef956b.x: The Council has only a delaying power (3 months, then 1 month), after which the Assembly's will prevails.

ndd39d7e8a40.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly?
o: The Deputy Speaker acts with full powers when the Speaker's office is vacant
The Speaker can be removed by a majority of all the then members after 14 days' notice
On dissolution, the Speaker continues until just before the new Assembly first meets
The Speaker addresses the resignation to the Governor
ndd39d7e8a40.x: Under Article 179 the Speaker resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker, not the Governor.

n78b0105eb9b.s:
Assertion (A): Article 169 deals with the creation or abolition of State Legislative Councils.
Reason (R): Article 202 deals with the Annual Financial Statement of a State.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n78b0105eb9b.x: Article 169 concerns Legislative Councils and Article 202 the Annual Financial Statement; both are true but unrelated.

na626b604ee5.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
na626b604ee5.s: Which Article bars discussion in the State Legislature of the conduct of a High Court judge in the discharge of duties?
na626b604ee5.x: Article 211 bars such discussion; Article 208 covers rules of procedure and Article 212 bars courts inquiring into proceedings.

nec3214bae40.s: Who is the Chairman of the Telangana Legislative Council?
nec3214bae40.x: Gutha Sukender Reddy is the Council Chairman; Gaddam Prasad Kumar is the Speaker of the Assembly.

nindian-polity-39-4.s: The maximum strength of a State Legislative Assembly is:
nindian-polity-39-4.x: An Assembly can have at most 500 and at least 60 members; Uttar Pradesh has the largest and Sikkim the smallest.

nindian-polity-40-37.s: The Legislative Council's power to delay ordinary Bills is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-40-37.x: Article 197 covers the Council's delay of ordinary Bills; 176 is the Governor's address and 207 the recommendation for Money Bills.

n81ddf2fa71a.s: The Governor's right to address and send messages to the House or Houses of the State Legislature is under Article:
n81ddf2fa71a.x: Article 175 covers the address and messages; 174 deals with sessions and dissolution and 176 with the special address.

nindian-polity-60-7.s: The term of a member of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-60-7.x: Council members serve six years, with one-third retiring every two years; the Council is a permanent body.

nc6d0e21fe86.s: A law of Parliament under Article 169 creating or abolishing a Legislative Council is passed by:
o: Two-thirds of members present and voting
A special majority with ratification by half the States
nc6d0e21fe86.x: Parliament uses a simple majority, and such a law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368.

nindian-polity-60-17.s: In a bicameral State Legislature, a Money Bill can be introduced only in:
nindian-polity-60-17.x: Money Bills start only in the Legislative Assembly; the Assembly is dissolvable with a five-year term, while the Council is permanent.

n2664a67c42d.s: The Governor nominates what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
n2664a67c42d.x: The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Council from literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service, on Cabinet advice.

nindian-polity-45-15.s: The minimum strength of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-45-15.x: A Council must have at least 40 members; one-third are elected by MLAs, one-twelfth by graduates and one-sixth nominated.

nindian-polity-60-5.s: The minimum age for membership of a State Legislative Council is:
nindian-polity-60-5.x: The minimum age is 30 for the Council (Article 171) and 25 for the Assembly (Article 170).

n8fee094ddc9.s: A Bill originating in the Legislative Council and rejected by the Legislative Assembly:
o: Is referred to a joint sitting
Returns to the Council for reconsideration
n8fee094ddc9.x: Such a Bill ends; the Council has no second chance and State Legislatures have no joint sitting.

n5958aa9e23c.s: The membership of a State Legislative Council cannot exceed ____ of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly.
n5958aa9e23c.x: A Council cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength nor be less than 40; Parliament fixes its actual strength.

ne0eb96fbc5e.s: The Legislative Assemblies of Goa and Mizoram have how many seats each?
ne0eb96fbc5e.x: Goa and Mizoram have 40 seats each, and Sikkim has 32 under Article 371F.

nindian-polity-40-8.s: Which Constitutional Amendment ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members under Article 333?
nindian-polity-40-8.x: The 104th Amendment Act, 2020 ended Anglo-Indian nomination; the 106th (2023) provides about one-third reservation for women.

nindian-polity-60-30.s: Which of the following has a Legislative Assembly of 40 seats or fewer but is NOT a State?
nindian-polity-60-30.x: Puducherry (33 seats) is a Union Territory; Goa and Mizoram (40 each) and Sikkim (32) are States.

nindian-polity-40-55.s: The minimum strength of a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is:
nindian-polity-40-55.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) caps a State ministry at 15% of the Assembly with a minimum of 12.

nindian-polity-60-11.s: An extension of a State Assembly's term during a National Emergency cannot continue beyond ____ after the Emergency ceases.
nindian-polity-60-11.x: Parliament may extend the term a year at a time during an Emergency, but not beyond six months after it ceases.

nindian-polity-62-18.s: On first passage, the Legislative Council can delay an ordinary Bill passed by the Assembly for a maximum of:
nindian-polity-62-18.x: The Council can delay an ordinary Bill three months, then one month after it is repassed; it has no veto.

nindian-polity-40-15.s: The Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly can vote:
o: Only a casting vote in case of a tie
In the first instance and also a casting vote
nindian-polity-40-15.x: The Speaker has only a casting vote when votes are tied, not a first vote.

nindian-polity-36-35.s: Teachers elect what fraction of the members of a State Legislative Council?
nindian-polity-36-35.x: Teachers and graduates each elect one-twelfth; one-sixth are nominated by the Governor.

nindian-polity-45-12.s: The representatives of a State in the Rajya Sabha are elected by:
nindian-polity-45-12.x: Elected MLAs choose them by PR-STV through secret ballot; nominated MLAs cannot vote.

nindian-polity-62-17.s: The Legislative Council must return a State Money Bill with its recommendations within:
nindian-polity-62-17.x: The Council must return a Money Bill within 14 days, failing which it is deemed passed by both Houses.

nindian-polity-40-57.s: Under the Tenth Schedule, defection cases arising in a State Legislative Council are decided by the:
nindian-polity-40-57.x: The Chairman decides defection cases in the Council under the Tenth Schedule.

nindian-polity-40-7.s: Which State has the smallest Legislative Assembly?
nindian-polity-40-7.x: Sikkim has the smallest State Assembly with 32 members; Puducherry has the smallest UT Assembly (33).

nindian-polity-21-27.s: State Money Bills are governed by Articles 198, 199 and:
nindian-polity-21-27.x: State Money Bills come under Articles 198, 199 and 207; Articles 200 and 201 concern reservation of Bills.

nindian-polity-39-31.s: The term of office of a Governor is:
nindian-polity-39-31.x: The Governor's term is five years, subject to the President's pleasure, and continues until a successor takes over.

nindian-polity-62-43.s: Which field is valid for nomination to a State Legislative Council but not to the Rajya Sabha?
nindian-polity-62-43.x: Under Article 80 the Rajya Sabha fields are literature, science, art and social service; the co-operative movement applies only to the Council.

nindian-polity-25-7.s: Under Article 103, the President decides the disqualification of a Member of Parliament on the opinion of the:
nindian-polity-25-7.x: The President acts on the ECI's binding opinion (Article 103); the Governor does the same for State legislators (Article 192).

n41418c135b9.s: Elected members of a State Legislative Assembly take part in the election of:
o: Both the President and the Vice-President
n41418c135b9.x: Elected MLAs are in the President's electoral college (Article 54); the Vice-President is elected only by MPs.

n9951f8c9d7d.s: Disqualification of a State legislator on grounds other than defection is decided by:
o: The Governor, bound by the Election Commission's opinion
n9951f8c9d7d.x: Under Articles 191–192 the Governor decides according to the Election Commission's opinion; defection goes to the Speaker or Chairman.

nindian-polity-62-11.s: A State Assembly resolution for creation or abolition of a Legislative Council must be passed by:
o: A simple majority of members present
A majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
Three-fourths of members present and voting
nindian-polity-62-11.x: It needs a special majority (majority of total membership and two-thirds present and voting), but only requests and does not compel the Union.

nb85164cdeb3.s: While a resolution for his removal is under consideration, the Speaker of a State Assembly:
o: Presides and has only a casting vote
Does not preside, but may speak and vote in the first instance
Must leave the House and cannot take part
Cannot speak but may vote in the second instance
nb85164cdeb3.x: Under Article 181 the Speaker does not preside but may speak and vote in the first instance.

ne0e8a491185.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed increase in Assembly seats under Section 26 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: The proposed strength for Telangana is 153
The increase has already been implemented
The proposed strength for Andhra Pradesh is 225
The increase is subject to Article 170
ne0e8a491185.x: Section 26 contemplates 225 seats for AP and 153 for Telangana subject to Article 170, but the increase has not yet been implemented.

n879c0948325.s:
Assertion (A): In Andhra Pradesh, the Committee on Public Undertakings replaces the Estimates Committee and the Public Accounts Committee.
Reason (R): Estimates Committees and Public Accounts Committees help ensure that grants are properly used.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n879c0948325.x: AP has the Committee on Public Undertakings in addition to, not instead of, the Estimates and Public Accounts Committees; R is true.

nc6f7fa0f86b.s: Which of the following pairs regarding the seat of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly is correctly matched?
o: Common-capital sessions before the move to Amaravati – Kurnool
Common-capital sessions before the move to Amaravati – Visakhapatnam
nc6f7fa0f86b.x: Before 1956 the Andhra State Assembly met at Kurnool; sessions were later held in Hyderabad, the common capital, until the move to Amaravati.

na8e079bb6e0.s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 deals with continuance of the AP Speaker and transfer of the Deputy Speaker?
na8e079bb6e0.x: Section 21 deals with the presiding officers; Sections 17, 19 and 20 deal with seats, sitting MLAs and the five-year term.

n4978208a864.s: Which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 relates to orders on Legislative Council constituencies?
n4978208a864.x: Section 24 concerns Council constituencies; Section 18 provided an Anglo-Indian nominee and Section 20 the five-year term.

n6392160b4c5.s: Who was the first Leader of Opposition in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
n6392160b4c5.x: Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first Leader of Opposition; Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker and Madapati Hanumantha Rao the first Council Chairman.

nfd5aa0de05e.s: The Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council, abolished in 1985, was revived in:
nfd5aa0de05e.x: The Council was created in 1958, abolished in 1985, revived in 2007, and an abolition resolution was passed in January 2020.

nfb8bd033837.s: After bifurcation, under Section 25 of the AP Reorganisation Act, the Chairman of the united AP Legislative Council:
o: Became Deputy Chairman of the AP Council
Continued as Chairman of the AP Council
Was replaced through a fresh election
nfb8bd033837.x: The Chairman continued as Chairman of the AP Council, while the Deputy Chairman went to Telangana's Council.

n8d0a1be89ee.s: Under the 2008 delimitation, which of the following AP districts has the highest number of Assembly constituencies?
n8d0a1be89ee.x: East Godavari has 19 Assembly constituencies, the highest among these districts.

nindian-polity-30-14.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched regarding the Supreme Court?
o: Ad hoc judge – Appointed by the CJI with the President's prior consent
Retired judge sitting – Requested by the CJI with the President's prior consent
Acting Chief Justice – Appointed by the President
Removal of a judge – Order by the CJI after an address by Parliament
nindian-polity-30-14.x: Removal is by an order of the President after an address by Parliament, not by the CJI.

nindian-polity-30-20.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about an ad hoc judge of the Supreme Court?
o: The previous consent of the President is required
The Chief Justice of the concerned High Court is consulted
Such a judge is appointed to meet a lack of quorum
Such a judge is appointed by the President on the collegium's advice
nindian-polity-30-20.x: The CJI appoints an ad hoc judge with the President's consent; appointment by the President on collegium advice applies to regular judges.

nf98fe3b488a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about recommendations on judicial appointments?
o: The Law Commission's 214th Report was submitted in 1998
A 2023 Standing Committee sought MoP changes for women and marginalised candidates
The 14th Report favoured appointing members of the Bar directly to the Supreme Court
The Law Commission's 14th Report was submitted in 1958
nf98fe3b488a.x: The 214th Report was submitted in 2008, not 1998.

nebb79a568c2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct when comparing the Supreme Court of India with the US Supreme Court?
o: India's Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143
India's appellate jurisdiction includes special leave under Article 136
The US Supreme Court has a writ jurisdiction equivalent to Article 32
The US Supreme Court lacks advisory jurisdiction
nebb79a568c2.x: The key marks the claim of an Article 32-equivalent writ jurisdiction in the US Supreme Court as false.

n62114caf431.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
n62114caf431.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 raised the number of judges other than the CJI from thirty-three to:
n62114caf431.x: The Ordinance, notified on 16 May 2026 under Article 123, replaced 'thirty-three' with 'thirty-seven', making total strength 38.

n2cff86e86f6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about a retired judge sitting in the Supreme Court under Article 128?
o: The consent of the retired judge is required
Such a judge exercises all the powers of a Supreme Court judge
The CJI requires the President's previous consent
Such a judge is deemed a regular judge of the Court for all purposes
n2cff86e86f6.x: Such a judge has the powers of a Supreme Court judge but is not deemed a regular judge of the Court.

n1da6b9fa944.s: Which of the following disputes does NOT fall within the Supreme Court's exclusive original jurisdiction under Article 131?
o: Between the Government of India and one or more States
Between the Union and some States on one side and other States on the other
Between two private companies incorporated in different States
n1da6b9fa944.x: Article 131 covers federal disputes only; a dispute between private companies is outside it.

nindian-polity-47-18.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched regarding the collegium system?
o: Supreme Court appointments – CJI and four senior-most SC judges
Formal appointing authority – President of India
High Court transfers – Chief Justice of the HC and two senior-most HC judges
High Court appointments – HC Chief Justice and two senior-most judges, forwarded to the SC Collegium
nindian-polity-47-18.x: High Court transfers involve the CJI, four senior-most SC judges and the Chief Justices of both High Courts.

nindian-polity-69-52.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about appeals to the Supreme Court?
o: Civil appeals under Article 133 need a High Court certificate
Constitutional appeals under Article 132 need a High Court certificate
Special leave under Article 136 needs a High Court certificate
An appeal under Article 134(1)(a) after a death sentence on reversal of acquittal lies as of right
nindian-polity-69-52.x: Special leave under Article 136 is granted at the Supreme Court's discretion and needs no High Court certificate.

n2630d2c8821.s: A person may be appointed a Supreme Court judge as a distinguished jurist if he is one in the opinion of the:
n2630d2c8821.x: The President's opinion governs the distinguished-jurist route, which has never been used; the person must be a citizen of India.

nindian-polity-69-51.s: The removal of a Supreme Court judge is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-69-51.x: Article 124(4) covers removal; 124(1) the number of judges, 124(2) retirement and 134A certificates for appeal.

n2830c9f65ad.s: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015), which judge was the lone dissent upholding the NJAC?
n2830c9f65ad.x: Justice J. Chelameswar dissented in the 4:1 verdict; the Bench was led by Justice J.S. Khehar.

n6607d0f9d6d.s: Which of the following falls outside the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court?
o: A dispute between two or more States
A dispute between the Union and one or more States
A dispute between the Union and some States against other States
n6607d0f9d6d.x: Election disputes concerning Parliament and State Legislatures go to the High Courts; federal disputes fall under Article 131.

nindian-polity-47-31.s: The Supreme Court Collegium for Supreme Court appointments consists of the CJI and:
o: Four senior-most judges and the Law Minister
nindian-polity-47-31.x: The collegium has five members, the CJI and four senior-most judges, with no executive member.

n76159bb54e7.s: The In-House Procedure (1999) for lesser misconduct in the higher judiciary followed which case?
n76159bb54e7.x: The In-House Procedure came after C. Ravichandran Iyer (1995) to handle misconduct not warranting removal.

nindian-polity-30-11.s: Under which Article is the Supreme Court a Court of Record?
nindian-polity-30-11.x: Article 129 makes it a Court of Record with power to punish contempt; Article 130 fixes its seat at Delhi.

n67249382eee.s: Who was to be the Chairperson of the National Judicial Appointments Commission?
o: The senior-most Supreme Court judge after the CJI
n67249382eee.x: The CJI was to chair the six-member NJAC; the Attorney-General was not a member.

n75a51370b4d.s: A retired High Court judge may plead only in:
o: The Supreme Court and other High Courts
n75a51370b4d.x: Article 220 permits practice only in the Supreme Court and other High Courts; Article 124(7) bars a retired SC judge altogether.

n6f677db2d54.s: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to pass orders necessary for doing complete justice?
n6f677db2d54.x: Article 142 is a power specific to the Supreme Court; High Courts have no equivalent under it.

n332efa53761.s: The transfer of a High Court Chief Justice is linked with Article:
n332efa53761.x: Transfer is under Article 222, while appointment is linked with Article 217(1).

n7f0b10a0f2c.s: If the collegium reiterates a recommendation returned by the Government, the Government:
o: May refer it to the President
Is bound to appoint the person
n7f0b10a0f2c.x: The Government may return a name once, but is bound to appoint if the collegium reiterates it.

nindian-polity-2-47.s: The advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court on a Presidential reference is under Article:
nindian-polity-2-47.x: Article 143 provides advisory jurisdiction; Article 141 makes the Supreme Court's law binding.

nindian-polity-71-21.s: A High Court judge retires at the age of:
nindian-polity-71-21.x: A High Court judge retires at 62 and a Supreme Court judge at 65.

nindian-polity-30-5.s: The appointment of ad hoc judges in the Supreme Court is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-30-5.x: Article 127 covers ad hoc judges; 126 the Acting CJI, 128 retired judges and 129 the Court of Record.

n33e5221e224.s: A motion for the removal of a judge must be signed by at least how many Lok Sabha members?
n33e5221e224.x: The motion needs 100 Lok Sabha members or 50 Rajya Sabha members.

nindian-polity-2-48.s: The appointment of District Judges is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-2-48.x: Article 233 covers District Judges; 215 makes High Courts Courts of Record, 216 constitutes them and 217 covers HC judges.

nindian-polity-2-13.s: The power of superintendence of High Courts is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-2-13.x: Article 227 gives superintendence; Article 226 is the High Court writ power.

n88105d66042.s: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgments?
n88105d66042.x: Article 137 provides review; Article 141 makes SC law binding and Article 142 allows orders for complete justice.

nf13078a4890.s: For taking judges out of office, the Constitution uses the term:
nf13078a4890.x: The Constitution uses 'removal', not 'impeachment', for judges.

n2c6291b605c.s: The Supreme Court of India is dealt with in which Part and Chapter of the Constitution?
n2c6291b605c.x: The Supreme Court is in Part V, Chapter IV (Articles 124–147).

nindian-polity-69-11.s: Civil appeals to the Supreme Court are governed by Article:
nindian-polity-69-11.x: Civil appeals are under Article 133; constitutional appeals 132, criminal 134 and special leave 136.

n07f7252894a.s: The Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah Commission (NCRWC), set up in 2000, submitted its report in:
n07f7252894a.x: The NCRWC submitted its report in 2002 and recommended a National Judicial Commission.

nindian-polity-69-33.s: The Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-69-33.x: Article 145(3) provides for the Constitution Bench.

n693fb314ef8.s: The 99th Constitutional Amendment (NJAC) received Presidential assent on:
n693fb314ef8.x: It was ratified by 16 States and assented to on 31 December 2014; the framework came into force on 13 April 2015.

nindian-polity-69-6.s: The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-69-6.x: Writs are under Article 32; original jurisdiction 131, review 137 and advisory 143.

ne6d7f663731.s: The pension of High Court Judges is charged on the:
ne6d7f663731.x: High Court salaries are charged on the State fund, but the pension is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

n5a1d0dcbff0.s: The collegium system of judicial appointments arises from:
n5a1d0dcbff0.x: The collegium is a judicial creation of the Three Judges Cases, with no express constitutional mention.

nindian-polity-69-26.s: An appeal under Article 134 where a High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death:
o: Lies without a High Court certificate
Lies only to a larger High Court bench
nindian-polity-69-26.x: Such an appeal lies as of right and needs no High Court certificate.

nindian-polity-47-15.s: Recommendations for High Court appointments are initiated by:
o: The High Court Chief Justice and two senior-most HC judges
nindian-polity-47-15.x: The proposal starts with the HC Chief Justice and two senior judges and goes to the CJI and two senior SC judges.

nebd97d2b15e.s: The process of appointing a High Court Chief Justice begins with a recommendation by:
o: The CJI and two senior-most Supreme Court judges
nebd97d2b15e.x: The CJI and two senior-most judges recommend first, followed by the Law Minister, the State, and appointment by the President.

nindian-polity-69-40.s: The curative petition rests on the Supreme Court's inherent powers anchored in Article:
nindian-polity-69-40.x: The curative petition, filed after dismissal of a review under Article 137, rests on inherent powers under Article 142.

nindian-polity-69-14.s: Under Article 145(3), a reference under Article 143 must be heard by a bench of at least:
nindian-polity-69-14.x: Article 145(3) requires at least five judges; the Article 143 opinion does not bind the President.

nindian-polity-69-13.s: The review jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 137 refers to its power to:
o: Review its own judgments or orders
Review High Court judgments on appeal
nindian-polity-69-13.x: Article 137 concerns review of the Court's own judgments, which differs from judicial review of statutes.

ncded906ef19.s: In which year did the Supreme Court shift to its building on Tilak Marg?
ncded906ef19.x: The Federal Court was set up in 1937, the Supreme Court was inaugurated in 1950 and shifted to Tilak Marg in 1958.

nindian-polity-30-6.s: The Second Judges Case was decided in:
nindian-polity-30-6.x: The First Judges Case was 1981, the Second 1993 and the Third 1998, before the NJAC (2014–15).

n99c474087b3.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 233 – Appointment of district judges by the Governor in consultation with the HC
Article 234 – Recruitment of other judicial officers after consulting the SPSC and the HC
Article 235 – Governor may apply these provisions to magistrates
Article 237 – Governor may apply these provisions to magistrates
n99c474087b3.x: Article 235 vests control over district and subordinate courts in the High Court; extension to magistrates is Article 237.

n877c17dcb1d.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
n877c17dcb1d.s: Which of the following is generally described as creative, proactive and reform-oriented?
n877c17dcb1d.x: Judicial activism is creative and reform-oriented, while judicial review is generally interpretative and legalistic.

nc0ec1225ba3.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Aravali Golf Club (2007) – Judges told not to encroach on legislative and executive functions
State of Rajasthan (1977) – Example of judicial restraint
State of Rajasthan (1977) – Declined to decide a political question
M.C. Mehta cases – Example of judicial restraint
nc0ec1225ba3.x: The M.C. Mehta cases are cited for court-issued policy directives, not judicial restraint.

n4f748bf4936.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 214 – A common High Court for two or more States
Article 217 – Appointment of High Court judges by the President
Article 230 – Extension or exclusion of HC jurisdiction over a Union Territory
Article 231 – A common High Court for two or more States
n4f748bf4936.x: Article 214 provides a High Court for each State; a common High Court is under Article 231.

n411299d2474.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about District Judges under Article 233?
o: The Governor appoints them in consultation with the High Court
A direct recruit needs seven years' standing as an advocate or pleader
A person already in Union or State service qualifies merely on seven years as an advocate
Article 233 deals with the appointment of District Judges
n411299d2474.x: Article 233 requires a direct recruit not to be already in the service of the Union or the State.

ne52a627041d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about proceedings against High Court judges?
o: Justice Soumitra Sen was a judge of the Calcutta High Court
Soumitra Sen resigned in 2011 after the Rajya Sabha voted for his removal
A motion against Justice G.R. Swaminathan was noticed by 107 MPs in December 2025
Yashwant Varma was formerly a judge of the Madras High Court
ne52a627041d.x: Yashwant Varma was formerly of the Allahabad High Court.

n1c259b2f33e.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 131 – High Court superintendence over subordinate courts
Article 143 – Advisory jurisdiction on a Presidential reference
Article 227 – High Court superintendence over subordinate courts
n1c259b2f33e.x: Article 131 is the Supreme Court's original jurisdiction in Centre-State disputes.

nindian-polity-51-25.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 137 – Supreme Court's review of its own judgments
Article 13(2) – Laws abridging Fundamental Rights void pro tanto
nindian-polity-51-25.x: Article 226 is High Court writ jurisdiction for Fundamental Rights and other legal rights; complete justice is Article 142.

naa1d289faf3.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Article 13 – Laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void
Article 32 – Supreme Court writs for Fundamental Rights
Article 137 – Supreme Court writs for Fundamental Rights
naa1d289faf3.x: Article 137 permits the Supreme Court to review its own judgments; Supreme Court writs are under Article 32.

n3b0508012e9.s: Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for court infrastructure, the normal Centre-State funding ratio is:
n3b0508012e9.x: The normal ratio is 60:40, 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States, and 100% for UTs; it is monitored on the Nyaya Vikas Portal.

nindian-polity-70-52.s: The oath or affirmation by High Court judges is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-70-52.x: Article 219 covers the oath; Article 220 restricts practice after retirement.

nc5087cd91ad.s: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution uses the expression:
nc5087cd91ad.x: Article 21 uses 'procedure established by law', while the US Constitution uses 'due process of law'.

n2bef84e52a0.s: Under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, wilful disobedience of a court's judgment or order is:
n2bef84e52a0.x: Civil contempt is wilful disobedience; criminal contempt covers scandalising or obstructing justice.

n524850eb381.s: Under which instrument of judicial activism does a court keep a case open to monitor compliance?
n524850eb381.x: Continuing mandamus keeps a case open to monitor compliance.

nindian-polity-70-18.s: Which High Court has jurisdiction over Puducherry?
nindian-polity-70-18.x: The Madras High Court covers Tamil Nadu and Puducherry; Kerala covers Lakshadweep.

neff3d00b841.s: Under Article 241, a High Court for a Union Territory may be constituted by:
neff3d00b841.x: Article 241 authorises Parliament by law to constitute a High Court for a UT; the President alone has no such power.

nf58017536c3.s: Article 224A, on retired judges sitting in High Courts, was inserted by the:
nf58017536c3.x: Article 224A was inserted by the 15th Amendment, 1963; additional judges fall under Article 224(1).

nindian-polity-70-14.s: Which Article applies certain Supreme Court removal provisions to High Court judges?
nindian-polity-70-14.x: Article 218 applies the Supreme Court's removal rules to High Court judges.

n5925fa9d0e0.s: A High Court consists of a Chief Justice and such other judges as may be deemed necessary by the:
n5925fa9d0e0.x: Article 216 leaves the number to the President; it fixes no uniform strength.

nc2da1a37c81.s: Which of the following is a criticism of judicial activism?
o: It has no effect on court workload
It may blur the separation of powers
nc2da1a37c81.x: Activism can blur separation of powers and overburden courts; wider access and executive accountability are its merits.

nf19351ac695.s: The appointment of an acting Chief Justice of a High Court is provided under Article:
nf19351ac695.x: Article 223 covers an acting Chief Justice; 224(1) additional judges, 224(2) acting judges and 224A retired judges.

nindian-polity-70-5.s: A common High Court for two or more States is provided under Article:
nindian-polity-70-5.x: Article 231 provides a common High Court; 222 covers transfer of judges.

ncd00f6e782c.s: In which country can courts not invalidate Acts of Parliament as in the US, because of parliamentary sovereignty?
ncd00f6e782c.x: Parliamentary sovereignty in the UK prevents US-style judicial review; Canada and Australia have judicial review.

n16ac91f3dda.s: Which 2024 case held that delimitation decisions can be reviewed if capricious?
n16ac91f3dda.x: Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod (2024) held delimitation review limited but possible if the decision is capricious.

nf6643842113.s: The re-enacted provisions of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 were struck down in 2025 in:
nf6643842113.x: The Act re-enacted conditions struck down earlier, and these were struck down again in Madras Bar Association (2025).

n12a03fb7982.s: The term 'judicial activism' was coined in 1947 by:
n12a03fb7982.x: Arthur Schlesinger Jr. coined the term in 1947; in India activism took root post-Emergency.

n43604a947e6.s: The Andhra State High Court was originally established at:
n43604a947e6.x: It was established at Guntur and shifted to Hyderabad on 1 November 1956.

nc8723b21816.s: The seat of the common High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh is at:
o: Leh in summer and Jammu in winter
Jammu in winter and Srinagar in summer
nc8723b21816.x: The common High Court sits at Jammu in winter and Srinagar in summer.

n721c9092471.s: The procedure for removal of a High Court judge is governed by the:
n721c9092471.x: Article 218 and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 govern removal; a Governor cannot remove a judge by executive order.

ne1353746c75.s: Which Article bars courts from inquiring into the advice of Ministers to the President?
ne1353746c75.x: Article 74(2) is the bar for advice to the President; Article 163(3) for advice to the Governor.

n945684323c6.shape: NOT (one-liner not buildable: original is a three-true set)
n945684323c6.s: Which of the following is NOT a concern raised in the recent debate on revisiting PIL jurisdiction?
o: Complete abolition of access to justice
n945684323c6.x: The debate concerns misuse, overreach and weak enforcement, not abolition of access to justice.

n9b902124fc2.s: The expression 'judicial review' in the Indian Constitution is:
o: Not used, though the power flows from several Articles
n9b902124fc2.x: The term is not used in the Constitution; the power flows from several Articles and is part of the basic structure.

nf81f093e256.s: A Public Interest Litigation before a High Court may be filed under Article:
nf81f093e256.x: PIL lies under Article 226 in High Courts and Article 32 in the Supreme Court.

nfe1ddc8d673.s: Judicial intervention that enters the executive or legislative domain and strains separation of powers is called:
nfe1ddc8d673.x: Judicial overreach occurs when courts enter the executive or legislative domain.

nf0b798bbad1.s: The separate High Court of Andhra Pradesh began functioning at Amaravati on:
nf0b798bbad1.x: It began on 1 January 2019 as India's 25th High Court; the Telangana High Court stayed at Hyderabad.

n6b7f9fb2b7c.x: Judicial dynamism is another term for judicial activism, the antithesis of judicial restraint.

ndea87e6465a.s: The National Judicial Academy is located at:
ndea87e6465a.x: The National Judicial Academy is at Bhopal; the AIJS (Article 312) has not yet been created.

na9e2302abd7.s: Which Article makes legislative power subject to the provisions of the Constitution?
na9e2302abd7.x: Article 245 makes legislative power subject to the Constitution; Articles 251 and 254 deal with repugnancy.

n574f495309b.s: The High Court collegium that initiates appointment proposals consists of the Chief Justice and the ____ senior-most judges of that High Court.
n574f495309b.x: The HC collegium is the Chief Justice plus two senior-most judges; the SC side is the CJI plus two senior-most judges.

n5c99fce80ce.s: The High Courts' power to review Central laws, barred by the 42nd Amendment, was restored by the:
n5c99fce80ce.x: The 43rd Amendment (1977) restored it; the 44th (1978) reversed the 38th Amendment's non-justiciability clauses.

neb4725acb0b.s: Under Article 217, a Judge of a High Court is appointed by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
neb4725acb0b.x: The President appoints after consulting the CJI, the Governor and, for a puisne judge, the HC Chief Justice.

n24de7ff182e.s: The first Lok Adalat camp was held in 1982 in:
n24de7ff182e.x: The first camp was in Gujarat in 1982; a Lok Adalat award is deemed a civil court decree and is final.

nf1d25a7e205.s: The Guwahati High Court has jurisdiction over Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and:
nf1d25a7e205.x: Guwahati covers Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh; Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura got their own HCs in 2013.

n98aa272cc87.s: The High Court's superintendence under Article 227 covers:
n98aa272cc87.x: Article 227 covers administrative and judicial superintendence and may be exercised suo motu.

nindian-polity-70-50.s: The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President after consultation with the:
o: CJI and the Union Law Minister
nindian-polity-70-50.x: For a HC Chief Justice the President consults the CJI and the Governor; for other judges also the HC Chief Justice.

neb827e7b0cc.s: In which year was privacy recognised as a fundamental right in Puttaswamy?
neb827e7b0cc.x: Puttaswamy (2017) came after post-Emergency activism, the expansion of Article 21 and governance cases like 2G.

nindian-polity-70-41.s: The strength of the Supreme Court is determined by:
nindian-polity-70-41.x: Under Article 124(1) Parliament fixes the Supreme Court's strength by law; under Article 216 the President fixes a High Court's.

nindian-polity-70-3.s: The first three High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were established in:
nindian-polity-70-3.x: The presidency High Courts came in 1862, then Agra (1866), which moved to Allahabad in 1869.

ndd6f3f5b501.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Tribunals Commission proposed in the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026?
o: Its Chairperson must be a serving judge of the Supreme Court
Its headquarters is proposed at New Delhi
Its functions include appointments, performance review and disciplinary inquiries
It is to have two judicial and two technical members besides the Chairperson
ndd6f3f5b501.x: The Chairperson may be a former Supreme Court judge or a former High Court Chief Justice, not necessarily a serving SC judge.

nd3124fd7c6a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about tribunals?
o: They are intended to provide faster adjudication
They bring specialised expertise into dispute resolution
Parent ministries may face a conflict of interest in administering them
They are completely outside the supervisory jurisdiction of constitutional courts
nd3124fd7c6a.x: Tribunals remain subject to judicial review by the High Courts.

n23d451c5fa5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 323A and 323B?
o: Article 323A permits Parliament and State Legislatures to legislate equally
Article 323A deals with recruitment and service conditions of public servants
Article 323B covers subjects such as taxation, foreign exchange and industrial disputes
Article 323B permits a hierarchy of tribunals
n23d451c5fa5.x: Under Article 323A, Parliament alone can legislate.

n8689fc24153.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Supreme Court's Madras Bar Association ruling of November 2025?
o: It struck down the four-year tenure for tribunal members
It ordered a National Tribunals Commission within four months
It struck down the minimum appointment age of 50 for tribunal members
It required the Search-cum-Selection Committee to send two names per vacancy
n8689fc24153.x: The two-name arrangement was struck down; it is now one name per vacancy.

nindian-polity-72-15.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: IMDT tribunals – Determination of illegal migrants
CAT – Union civil servants' service matters
TDSAT – Telecom, broadcasting and airport tariff disputes
nindian-polity-72-15.x: The NGT hears environmental disputes; IMDT tribunals decided who was an illegal migrant.

n27674c5fd84.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal was established in:

nc149e0c30fb.s: Tribunals for elections and foodstuffs are associated with Article:
nc149e0c30fb.x: Elections and foodstuffs fall under Article 323B; Article 323A covers service matters with one tribunal for the Centre and each State.

nindian-polity-72-28.s: Tribunals under Article 323A can be established by:
nindian-polity-72-28.x: Only Parliament can act under Article 323A; both Parliament and States can act under 323B.

n8fb1ec8781f.s: Which of the following is NOT a merit of administrative tribunals?
o: Compulsory application of the full Civil Procedure Code
n8fb1ec8781f.x: Tribunals follow natural justice rather than the full Civil Procedure Code; expertise, speed and lower cost are their merits.

n2be13c67128.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal has no original jurisdiction over service disputes of:
n2be13c67128.x: CAT covers Central civil servants, AIS officers and civilian defence employees, not private-sector employees.

n145cb828627.s: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 was passed by the Lok Sabha on 10 August 2026 and by the Rajya Sabha on:
n145cb828627.x: It passed the Rajya Sabha on 11 August 2026; it repeals the 2021 Act and creates a National Tribunals Commission.

nea239d12679.s: Articles 323A and 323B (Part XIV-A) were inserted by the:
nea239d12679.x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted them, following the Swaran Singh Committee; the 75th Amendment added the rent and tenancy clause.

nff5dd3bc5ef.s: The Principal Bench of the Armed Forces Tribunal is located at:
nff5dd3bc5ef.x: The Principal Bench is at New Delhi; Jaipur, Jabalpur and Guwahati have Regional Benches.

nindian-polity-72-5.s: Which case held that judicial review by High Courts (Articles 226/227) and the Supreme Court (Article 32) is part of the Basic Structure?
nindian-polity-72-5.x: L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997) so held.

nindian-polity-72-14.s: Cyber appellate orders of TDSAT lie before the:
nindian-polity-72-14.x: TDSAT decides telecom, broadcasting and airport tariff disputes; its cyber appellate orders go to the High Court.

nindian-polity-72-41.s: Part XIV-A of the Constitution deals with:
o: Services under the Union and the States
nindian-polity-72-41.x: Part XIV-A covers tribunals; services are in Part XIV, co-operatives in IX-B and Municipalities in IX-A.

n91cdc04c1f7.s: In relation to the High Courts, tribunals:
o: Supplement them but do not replace them
n91cdc04c1f7.x: Because judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 is basic structure, tribunals supplement but cannot replace the High Courts.

nindian-polity-51-10.s: Judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 cannot be abrogated by Parliament even through Article:
nindian-polity-51-10.x: Being part of the basic structure, judicial review cannot be removed even by amendment under Article 368.

nindian-polity-50-45.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: President's modification of revenue distribution – Ceases six months after the Emergency is revoked
Proclamation of National Emergency – Requires written advice of the Union Cabinet
Parliament's laws on State List subjects – Cease six months after the Emergency is revoked
nindian-polity-50-45.x: Revenue modification lasts until the end of the financial year in which the proclamation ceases.

ndb170477b45.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian federal structure?
o: The Constitution provides completely separate judicial and administrative machinery for every State
The Supreme Court is an independent adjudicator in Centre-State disputes
The Constitution provides for two sets of governments
The Constitution is written and supreme
ndb170477b45.x: India has an integrated judicial and administrative framework, not separate machinery for every State.

n979d66e4161.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about amendment of the Indian Constitution?
o: The Constitution is neither wholly rigid nor wholly flexible
Most provisions can be amended by Parliament without State ratification
Certain federal provisions need ratification by at least half the State Legislatures
n979d66e4161.x: The Constitution is neither wholly rigid nor wholly flexible.

n40200d56161.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Forty-fourth Amendment?
o: Emergency must be proclaimed on the Union Cabinet's written advice
One-tenth of Lok Sabha members can require a special sitting within 14 days to consider disapproval
It reduced the approval period for National Emergency to one month
It retained 'internal disturbance' as a ground for Emergency
n40200d56161.x: The 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion'.

n6c2d20204e2.shape: one-liner (NOT not buildable: all original statements are true)
n6c2d20204e2.s: Which single authority audits both Union and State accounts, regarded as a unitary feature?
n6c2d20204e2.x: A single CAG auditing Union and State accounts, central appointment of Governors, AIS control and emergency powers are unitary features.

n2d0b5ebf1dd.s:
Assertion (A): The State of Jammu and Kashmir had a separate constitution and flag.
Reason (R): The former Article 370 provided special arrangements for the State.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2d0b5ebf1dd.x: Article 370 provided the special arrangements, including a separate constitution and flag; they were made inoperative in August 2019.

n6ff40310948.s:
Assertion (A): The 42nd Amendment moved the constitution and organisation of the Supreme Court and High Courts to the Concurrent List.
Reason (R): The 42nd Amendment moved five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n6ff40310948.x: The administration of justice entry moved covers courts other than the Supreme Court and High Courts, so A is false; R is true.

n7ffe93491de.s:
Assertion (A): Granville Austin described Indian federalism as cooperative federalism.
Reason (R): Ivor Jennings described India as a federation with a strong centralising tendency.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n7ffe93491de.x: Both descriptions are correctly attributed, but one scholar's view does not explain the other's.

n4c7a2b9f002.s: The Constitution describes India as a:
n4c7a2b9f002.x: India is a 'Union of States'; the Constitution does not use 'Federation of States'.

n80a7b8847bf.s: The Inter-State Council was set up in:
n80a7b8847bf.x: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990, during the 1989–2014 coalition era.

nca9456a0743.s: Entry 92A in the Seventh Schedule was inserted by the:
nca9456a0743.x: Entry 92A was inserted by the Sixth Amendment, 1956; inserted entries make counts differ from last entry numbers.

n26a3e3f9e84.s: A proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 must be approved by Parliament within:
n26a3e3f9e84.x: Article 352 needs approval within one month; Articles 356 and 360 within two months by simple majority.

n33ea934685c.s: The constitution and organisation of High Courts is a subject in the:
n33ea934685c.x: It is a Union subject; defence is Union, taxes on mineral rights State, and social security Concurrent.

nindian-polity-50-19.s: Parliamentary approval of a National Emergency requires:
o: A special majority in both Houses
A special majority in the Lok Sabha only
A simple majority in both Houses
nindian-polity-50-19.x: A National Emergency needs a special majority; President's Rule and Financial Emergency need simple majorities.

nda5c88caf02.s: In Mineral Area Development Authority v. SAIL, the nine-judge Bench held by majority that royalty:
o: Is a fee under the Union List
Can be levied only by the Union
nda5c88caf02.x: The 8:1 majority held royalty is not a tax and recognised that States can tax mineral rights.

n5d8f291edcc.s: The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from:
n5d8f291edcc.x: The Concurrent List came from Australia; the strong Centre from Canada and the federal scheme from the 1935 Act.

n9a8a0f3c5c8.s: A Bill under Article 3 to alter the boundaries of a State can be introduced only on the recommendation of the:
n9a8a0f3c5c8.x: An Article 3 Bill needs the President's recommendation and is referred to the State legislature, whose views do not bind Parliament.

n3183497027c.s: Financial Emergency is provided for under Article:
n3183497027c.x: Financial Emergency is under Article 360, not Article 311.

n81feb1ce771.s: Who described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'?
n81feb1ce771.x: K.C. Wheare called it quasi-federal; Morris Jones used 'bargaining federalism' and Austin 'cooperative federalism'.

nindian-polity-50-8.s: How many times has a National Emergency been proclaimed in India?
nindian-polity-50-8.x: National Emergencies were declared in 1962, 1971 and 1975; a Financial Emergency has never been declared.

n3da7fbb4952.s: Officers of the All India Services are recruited through the:
n3da7fbb4952.x: AIS officers are recruited through the UPSC and serve both the Union and the States under central control.

nfcdb2f8395d.s: The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister is collectively responsible to the:
nfcdb2f8395d.x: Under Articles 74(1) and 75 the Council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; the President is the nominal head.

ndef78c0cd29.s: The allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States is provided in the:
ndef78c0cd29.x: Seats are allotted broadly by population in the Fourth Schedule, unlike equal representation in the US Senate.

nindian-polity-51-13.s: Which of the following is part of judicial review?
o: Questioning the political wisdom of legislation
Examining the constitutionality of executive orders
nindian-polity-51-13.x: Testing executive orders is part of judicial review; it does not question political wisdom, pre-screen Bills or act as an appeal.

nindian-polity-68-20.s: Corporation Tax is placed in the Union List at Entry:
nindian-polity-68-20.x: Corporation Tax is Union List Entry 85; inter-State trade and commerce is Entry 42.

nindian-polity-50-9.s: Which of the following can happen during a Financial Emergency?
o: Financial directions are given and salaries may be reduced
Parliament legislates on State List subjects
nindian-polity-50-9.x: In a Financial Emergency, financial directions can be given and pay cut; State Budgets are passed by Parliament under President's Rule.

nb742f99943d.s: Which of the following is a unitary feature of the Indian Constitution?
nb742f99943d.x: Single citizenship is a unitary feature; dual polity and bicameralism are federal features.

n77f1a7bc937.s: Which case recognised federalism as part of the basic structure and opened Article 356 proclamations to judicial review?
n77f1a7bc937.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) recognised federalism as basic structure and limited misuse of Article 356.

nd7e50b9fff7.s: A law under Article 3 to form a new State is passed by:
o: A special majority with State ratification
nd7e50b9fff7.x: Article 3 laws need only a simple majority.

na15213077f6.s: The expression 'Union of India' refers to:
na15213077f6.x: The Union of India refers to the States; the Territory of India also includes UTs and acquired territories.

nindian-polity-50-18.s: The 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' in Article 352 with:
nindian-polity-50-18.x: It substituted 'armed rebellion', cut approval to one month, protected Articles 20–21 and required the Cabinet's written advice.

nindian-polity-68-42.s: Stock exchanges and futures markets fall in the:
nindian-polity-68-42.x: Stock exchanges, banking, foreign affairs and inter-State migration are all Union List subjects.

nindian-polity-68-36.s: Radio and television broadcasting is a subject in the:
nindian-polity-68-36.x: Broadcasting is a Union subject, while agriculture, land and fisheries are State subjects.

nindian-polity-68-17.s: Price control is a subject in the:
nindian-polity-68-17.x: Price control and economic and social planning are Concurrent subjects; census is Union and railway police is State.

nindian-polity-50-28.s: If the Lok Sabha is dissolved before approving an Emergency proclamation already approved by the Rajya Sabha, it survives until ____ from the new Lok Sabha's first sitting.
nindian-polity-50-28.x: The 30-day rule applies to National Emergency, President's Rule and Financial Emergency alike.

nindian-polity-50-13.s: Parliament's laws on State List subjects during a National Emergency cease to operate ____ after it is revoked.
nindian-polity-50-13.x: Such laws lapse six months after the Emergency ends.

nindian-polity-68-50.s: Population control and family planning was inserted in the Concurrent List as Entry:
nindian-polity-68-50.x: Entry 20A was added by the 42nd Amendment, which also moved administration of justice to the Concurrent List.

nindian-polity-50-43.s: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and States under Article:
nindian-polity-50-43.x: Article 354 allows it; the change lasts until the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends.

n683da91c356.s: The coalition era of Indian federalism, with more negotiated Centre-State relations, broadly spanned:
n683da91c356.x: Congress dominance (1952–67), confrontation (1967–77), the Janata interlude (1977–89) and the coalition era (1989–2014).

nindian-polity-50-16.s: The last National Emergency was formally withdrawn on 21 March:
nindian-polity-50-16.x: Emergencies were declared in 1962, 1971 and 1975; the last was lifted on 21 March 1977.

o: A destructible Union of destructible States
An indestructible Union of indestructible States
An indestructible Union of destructible States
A destructible Union of indestructible States
n4f8502dc5af.x: India is an indestructible Union of destructible States; the US is an indestructible Union of indestructible States.

n69d7795d372.s: 'Federal in structure with unitary features' best describes the constitutional system of:
n69d7795d372.x: India is described as federal in structure with unitary features and as a Union of States.
